items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-09-01
items.q: I'd get in bands like with Snagg Jones and all them kind of fellows playing by head.

ctx.x: Punch, in 1919, when you first got here, what did the brass bands play like? Were they strictly music? Were they here?

No, they played more marches then. But I'm going to tell you now, I ain't going to lie to you. Hick was a very few men's in them bands reading. Like the trumpet players be reading. But them other guys were just speaking. I mean, you know, using their brains. They could hear a tune and play it. That's right. Yeah. That's right. Now you take men like Joe Howard, and them men that were playing. They had their music up. They were playing it, see? But they had men on trombone, men on alto, and things like that. They…
Well, what about Louie? Did you ever work with him?
